steps: Unpack & initial assembly

Fit fuel conversion and firebox panels before lifting the stove off the pallet. Open the firebox with the latch tool, check the hardware kit, then install the 4 AA backup batteries and 3 AAA in the transmitter.

1. Enamel stoves only: lift off the top plate and remove and discard the door-stop bolt from the hinge bar (10mm wrench, fig. 2.1).
  2. Open the firebox: the front door swings open to the left. Lift off the top plate grills and top plate. Use the latch tool from the shipping pallet to pull the two latch hooks out of the glass frame, tilt the frame forward and lift it straight up and off.
  3. Remove the miscellaneous hardware kit from the firebox and check it against the list on p. 4.
  4. Install the four AA backup batteries in the battery box in the controls compartment, polarity per the box label. Fit 3 AAA batteries in the transmitter; it is synchronized with the appliance at the factory.
  5. Optional equipment and burner media: sections 11 and 12.
For easiest access, install fuel conversion and firebox panels before removing the stove from the pallet. Don't drag the legs; have help moving it, and set removed enamel parts on a blanket or towel. Re-install the top plate before connecting vent pipe.
Location & clearances

Plan for heat distribution, vent termination, gas line routing and traffic. Hold the stove, alcove and mantel clearances; floor protection on any combustible floor other than wood, never directly on carpeting, vinyl or linoleum.
Vent system & exhaust restrictor
One approved vent maker only, inner joints sealed with a 1/8" bead of high-temperature sealant or Mil-Pac (no silicone). Set the exhaust restrictor dial to the termination zone from the vent matrix.

Approved vent systems: M&G DuraVent DirectVent Pro and GS Series; American Metal Products (Amerivent); Security Chimneys International (Secure Vent); Selkirk Metalbestos (Direct Temp); Metal-Fab (Sure-Seal Direct Vent); Industrial Chimney Corp. (ExcelDirect); Bernard Dalsin Mfg. (Pro Form); Olympia Chimney Supply (Ventis Direct Vent). Don't mix components from different manufacturers. Never modify any vent part or use any damaged venting product.

Vent directly outside on its own system: never into a chimney serving a solid fuel or gas appliance; common vents are prohibited. Seal the male section of each inner pipe with a 1/8" bead of high-temperature sealant or Mil-Pac. Do not use silicone sealant.

Exhaust restrictor

The plate in the firebox exhaust outlet prevents overly strong draft, which causes poor combustion and a weak flame picture. The dial runs from the factory-set fully open position to approximately 70% restricted; lettered positions A, B, C, D match the termination zones of the vent matrix, which is a diagram (fig. 6.2, p. 10). Loosen the lock nut with a 10 mm open-end wrench, set the dial with the pivot tab, retighten. On a zone division line use the less restrictive position: termination 10 feet high and offset 7 feet sets Position B.

Re-install the top plate before connecting vent to the stove. Long vertical runs (over 12 ft.) in uninsulated air space may need CPI mode for best performance.
Fuel conversion (propane)
Ships for natural gas. An authorized technician converts it with supplied kit 158057: injectors, LP shutter lock screw, baffle wings, regulator motor and labels, then leak and pressure checks.

1. Turn off the gas supply. Open the door, release the glass frame latches, tilt the frame forward and lift it out.
  2. In the controls compartment, loosen the air shutter wing nut below the firebox floor and push the stem back as far as it will travel.
  3. Lift the front of the burner base off its support brackets, pull it forward off the injector, tilt it side to side and pull it out through the door opening.
  4. Replace the burner injector with the kit injector (1/2" open-end wrench or deep-well socket). Do not over-tighten: it can damage the brass elbow and cause a gas leak.
  5. Propane only: install the 1/2" air shutter lock screw; it sets the new, minimal shutter opening.
  6. Pilot injector: remove the pilot shield screws (1/4" socket driver) and pilot head base (7/16" wrench), swap the injector, and orient the hood to project flame to the flame sensor and burner carry-over ports. Retighten the base nut; replace shield and rear skirt.
  7. Propane only: remove two 10 mm nuts to drop the exhaust baffle; loosen the two upper baffle nuts, break both end wings off at the perforations, retighten; replace the lower baffle.
  8. Refit the burner: level, and securely engaged with the front supports on the firebox floor.
  9. Pull the rating plates out, remove the #8 screws each side of the control cabinet and let the IFC hang. Disconnect the regulator motor lead from terminal "M", swap the regulator (Torx T-20), reconnect to "M", remount the IFC without crimping wires.
  10. Labels: A on the lower door hinge, B on the rating plate, the small label on the valve.
  11. Reassemble and apply gas. Leak-check with soapy water or a digital gas detector, never an open flame, without wetting the IFC. Confirm pressures with a manometer.
Installer note (p. 15): the pilot shield is removed for propane in a minimum vent run. For taller vents, or where high winds are present, it can remain installed if nuisance outages occur. Keep the shield.
Gas supply + leak test
Connect to the flex line behind the utility cover at the rear leg (3/8" npt, 1/2" diameter supply). Shut-off valve and union in the same room; leak-test every joint.

Supply line 3/8" npt with a 1/2" diameter supply, or the size that gives the valve sufficient pressure regardless of the input setting. Route it to the flex line behind the utility cover at the rear leg. Flexible gas appliance connectors are acceptable in many U.S. areas; Canadian methods vary by local code. Comply with local code, or ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 or CAN-B149.

  • Gas shut-off valve (gas cock) and union in the supply line, in the same room as the appliance. Massachusetts requires a T-handle gas cock (248CMR).
  • Seal joints with suitable compounds, propane-resistant on LP units.
  • Turn on the gas and test all joints for leaks.
Gas pressure & high altitude
Manometer on the valve test points (A manifold, B inlet), control knob on HIGH. Above 2000 feet, check whether the supplier derates before fitting a high altitude kit.

Valve test points (front of valve): A = manifold, B = inlet / supply. Always test with the valve control knob set on HIGH.

Inlet NG / LP5.0 – 7.0 / 11.0 – 14.0 in. WC
Manifold NG / LP1.6 – 3.5 / 6.4 – 10.0 in. WC

High altitude: most suppliers derate gas above 2000 feet; check first. If not, fit kit 158059 (propane) or 158060 (NG) using the burner-injector steps of the conversion, then repeat leak, pressure, system and flame checks. Orifices for 610-1370 meters (2000-4500 ft.): NG 2.30 mm, propane 1.40 mm. Fill out and apply the high altitude label to the rating plate.
Panels & burner media
Panel kits after any conversion kit, burner media last. Ember stones off the side and front ports and the pilot carry-over area; fire glass clear of the pilot; no more than 1/4 of the rock wool.

Panel kits (Skamol 158046 or black reflective glass 157965), after any fuel or high altitude kit: rear panel bottom first, behind the pilot assembly shield on the rear shelf; side panels on the shelves beside the burner, each held by a retainer tab pried down with a flat head screwdriver. Glass panels smooth side out, handled with the cotton gloves supplied.

Log set 158045: base log on the two burner-base pins; rest the right log in the small pocket on the base log and against the back corner; engage the hole in the left log's charred end on the base log pin and lean it into the back corner. Ember stones in a thin layer over the rear ports only, up to the rear flange, clear of the pilot carry-over area and the burner perimeter. Rock wool in small pinches over the front of the burner base: no more than 1/4 of the supply.

Other media: River Rock Set 158055 must engage the burner pins in the correct orientation (fig. 12.3a/b). Tumbled Stones 158054 in a single layer; flat stones must not completely block gas flow through the ports, and don't obstruct the air space between the burner perimeter and the burner skirt. Fire glass 156815 / 157342: no more than the four pounds supplied, crowned toward the center, nothing in front of the pilot assembly. Beach Fire Logset 158229: pp. 42–43.

Note: the log set contents list on p. 21 numbers the logs #2 Left Log (226265) and #3 Right Log (226266); the steps on the same page call them Right Log #2 and Left Log #3.
Propane in minimum vent configurations may soot: brush the logs and remove some or all of the rock wool.
System check
Purge the line, then check the pilot: steady, blue at the hood with yellow edges, engulfing the top 1/8" of the flame sensor. Confirm burner function at all heat levels.

1. Purge: the first lighting takes a few moments to clear air from the line. From a cold start it may help to let the pilot burn 10 - 15 minutes to establish positive draft before turning the burner on.
  2. Pilot flame (behind the burner, rear of the firebox): steady, not lifting or floating; blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow toward the outer edges; engulfs the top 1/8" of the flame sensor; projects toward the burner carry-over ports. Adjust with the screw left of the valve regulator, qualified technician only.
  3. The more offsets in the vent system, the greater the need for an air shutter adjustment (next step).

Once burner function is confirmed at all heat levels, the homeowner runs it several hours on low, then several hours on high, to cure the paint.
Air shutter & flame picture
From the mid-point of the range, burn 20-30 minutes on HIGH and open the shutter in 1/16" - 1/8" steps if the flame is weak, slow or sooty; tighten the wing nut.

Open the front door and the controls access door and loosen the wing nut. Slide the stud forward to open (more air), back to restrict.

  1. Start at the mid-point of the total range of adjustment.
  2. Burn 20-30 minutes on HIGH, watching the flame. If it looks weak, slow or sooty, open the shutter in 1/16" - 1/8" increments, letting the flames settle a few minutes after each change.
  3. Tighten the wing nut.

Too large an air setting: blue, transparent, "anemic" flame. Too small: very long yellow flames, black soot on the logs, firebox walls and possibly the exterior termination cap. Reference flame pictures: fig. 14.2 (log set) and p. 41 (other media), shown as photos.

Note: p. 24 says to open the air shutter if the flame looks weak, slow or sooty; the same page says too large an air setting gives a blue, transparent or "anemic" flame, and p. 9 says overly strong draft can cause poor combustion and a weak flame picture.

After converting back to natural gas, p. 18 instead says: start with the shutter open 1/16", run at least 15 minutes, then adjust in very small increments (1/16" - 1/8").

Note: the specifications on p. 4 give the factory air shutter settings as NG 0" and LP 1/16" open; the conversion section on p. 18 says the factory setting for NG is 1/16" open.
Mobile home (if applicable)
Secure to the floor and ground to the chassis with Floor Bracket Kit 158074; install to Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 (U.S.) or CSA Z240.4 (Canada).

1. Per local electrical code, run a ground wire from the mobile home grounding to the stove's rear leg location.
  2. Loosen the lower cover plate bolts on the rear leg and engage each kit floor bracket with a bolt head.
  3. Mark the bracket bolt holes on the floor and drill the fastener holes.
  4. Make the ground connection at a cover plate bolt or floor bolt; fasten the brackets to the floor and tighten the cover plate bolts.

Kit: two leg brackets. Also needed: drill and bit, adjustable wrench, lag screws (or similar) suited to the floor, grounding wire and chassis clamp. Check local restrictions first.

panels.title: Yellow, sooty flame
items: Very long yellow flames → air shutter setting too small
Black soot on logs, firebox walls or termination cap → incomplete combustion or too little combustion air at the shutter
Soot on propane in a minimum vent configuration → brush the logs; remove some or all rock wool

panels.title: Blue, transparent flame
items: Blue, transparent, "anemic" flame → air shutter setting too large; see the note under "Air shutter & flame picture"
Poor combustion, weak flame picture → overly strong draft; set the exhaust restrictor for the termination zone

panels.title: Pilot outages & lockout
items: No rectification after four attempts → lockout; clear by cancelling the call for heat
Unstable or weak draft (warm weather, extreme cold, long vent run, high wind) → run in CPI
Nuisance outages on propane with taller vents or high winds → pilot shield can remain installed
Poor draft or draft reversal (steep roof, nearby trees, wind) → increasing vent height may help
Poor pilot ignition with fire glass → keep the carry-over ports in front of the pilot clear

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
An ignition device lights the pilot automatically, so never try to light it by hand. The Mode switch (also called the burner switch) is in the controls compartment under the firebox: press the control access door to release its catch and swing it down.

  1. Check the stove is connected to 120VAC house current.
  2. Set the thermostat, if you use one, to its lowest setting, and the Mode switch to OFF.
  3. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. Then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and see "Safety & gas smell."
  4. Set the Mode switch to REMOTE.
  5. Press ON/OFF on the remote. The pilot lights, followed shortly by the burner.

The first time, it takes a few moments to clear air from the gas line.

If it won't light: it tries four times, then locks out. Clear a lockout by switching the burner off or adjusting the thermostat. If it still won't operate, turn off the gas and call your service technician or gas supplier.

To turn off the gas: thermostat to its lowest setting, all electric power off if service is to be done, Mode switch to OFF, then close the control access door.

Note: p. 26 and p. 28 say the Mode switch's ON position lights the pilot and then the burner, which stays on until switched off; the lighting instructions on p. 45 say ON gives continuous pilot operation, with the burner lit from the remote.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote works when the stove's Mode switch is set to REMOTE. It's paired with the stove at the factory, and the stove beeps once to confirm each command.

  • ON/OFF turns the burner and accent lamp on or off. The pilot lights first, then the burner.
  • Up / Down sets one of six flame levels. Each press of Down lowers the flame a step, until the burner turns off. Press Up while the system is on but the flame is off, and the flame comes on at High.
  • Thermostat: press once to use the remote as a room thermostat, then set the temperature with Up / Down. Press until "SMART" appears for Smart mode, which turns the flame down as the room nears your set temperature.
  • Mode chooses what you control. With the remote on, step to the lamp icon: Up turns the accent lamp on, the arrows set brightness, Down turns it off.

Child lock: press Mode and Up together; do the same to unlock. °F or °C: with the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together.

The stove can turn on suddenly. Keep away from the burner when using the remote. On thermostat control it may be very hot even when the burner doesn't seem to be on. Keep the remote where children can't reach it.

If the remote malfunctions, turn the stove off with its main ON/OFF switch.

firstfire.title: Your first fires
firstfire.html:
The paint is air-dried at the factory but has to be heat-cured. That happens during the first firings, and it gives off an odor and some visible smoke. It's normal and temporary.

Before the first fire

  • Ventilate: open doors and windows and use a fan to move fresh air through the room.
  • Vacate: the fumes are non-toxic, but they can bother babies, small children, pregnant women, older people, pets and anyone with breathing difficulties. Keep them out of the room.

Curing

Once your installer has confirmed the burner works at all heat levels, run the stove on a low setting for several hours, then for several hours on a high setting.

Fog and white film on the glass

A little condensation fogs the glass each time you light it. It disappears as the glass heats. After the first few fires you'll also see a white, powdery film on the inside of the glass, left as the paint and burner media cure.

Clean that film off. Left on, it can permanently etch the glass. Use a non-abrasive hearth gas appliance glass cleaner or warm water, only on cool glass, and never an ammonia-based cleaner.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when it needs it, and only when it's cool.

  1. Wipe the surface with a clean, dampened, soft cloth.
  2. Follow with a dry, soft towel.
  3. Take care not to scratch the glass.
Never use abrasive cleaners or ammonia-based cleaning solutions, and never clean the glass while it's hot.

After the first few fires

Remove the white, powdery film with a non-abrasive hearth gas appliance glass cleaner and warm water. If it's left on, it can permanently etch the glass.

Check for damage

Scratches weaken the glass, so look for them. If you find any, the panel should be replaced, using only door glass kit 158067 and side glass panel 158080. Don't run the stove with any glass panel removed, cracked or broken. Replacement should be done only by a licensed or qualified service person.

Have the fire-glass burner media? It may discolor over time. Soaking it in a detergent bath brings back its original finish.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
The pilot is the small flame that lights the burner. It can work two ways:

IPI (default)intermittent pilot · lights only when there's a call for heat
CPIcontinuous pilot · stays lit

To switch: with the remote off, press Mode. IPI shows first. Press Up for CPI, or Down to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms it.

When CPI helps

If the draft is weak or unstable, the manual advises CPI. Warm weather, extreme cold, a long vent run and high wind can all interfere with IPI. A pilot that's always burning makes enough heat to help keep the draft going. Long vertical vent runs (over 12 ft.) in uninsulated air space may need CPI too.

With the pilot always lit, take care using household products that give off combustible vapors.

In CPI, the stove puts the pilot out automatically if there's no call for heat for 7 days.

Note: after the 7-day shut-off, p. 27 says the pilot switches to IPI and re-ignites by itself at the next call for heat, and p. 45 also says it re-ignites automatically; p. 28 says to follow the lighting instructions to relight it.

sounds.title: Sounds you'll hear
sounds.html:
Creaking and pinging

The cast iron and steel parts expand and contract as they heat up and cool down. The creaks and pings are that natural thermal movement, not a fault.

A low hum

If your stove has the optional blower fan, it hums slightly on its low setting. The sound grows as the fan moves more air.

Maker's website: Product feature: Standard features include accent light, blower fan, and remote control.

Beeps

The stove's receiver beeps once to confirm each command from the remote.

Sparking at start-up

When there's a call for heat, an electrode sparks to light the pilot. On the first try it can spark for up to 60 seconds before the burner lights.

An odor or a little smoke during the first fires is the paint curing: see "Your first fires." A gas smell is different: see "Safety & gas smell."

power.title: Power and batteries
power.html:
The stove runs on 120V house current. If the power goes out, a backup battery pack keeps the burner working from the remote.

Backup battery pack4 × AA, 1.5v each
Remote3 × AAA, 1.5V

On backup power only the burner functions work. The accent lamp stays off until the power is back.

Changing the backup AAs

A red light on the control board means the backup batteries are low. Shut off the main gas supply before removing or replacing batteries. Then:

  1. Disconnect electrical power from the stove.
  2. Remove the cast iron overlay.
  3. Open the battery box in the control compartment: slide the two cover sliders outward and pull out the holder.
  4. Fit four new AA batteries as the polarity marks on the box show, push the holder in and slide the sliders inward to lock.
  5. Reconnect power.

Changing the remote's AAAs

A battery icon appears on the remote's screen before the power runs out. Three fresh AAA batteries clear it. Avoid pressing the thermostat key while you do this, or the thermostat functions turn off; to restore them, re-install the batteries while pressing the thermostat key.

Note: p. 5 says the battery box is in the left side of the controls compartment; p. 34 says the right side.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance. Put out any open flame. Open windows.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building immediately.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the stove

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The built-in safety screens on the door and side glass must stay in place. If one is damaged, replace it only with Jøtul Front Replacement Screen 158062 or Side Replacement Screen 158063 from a Jøtul dealer.
  • Supervise young children in the room. A child guard or safety gate is recommended if at-risk people live in the house.
  • Keep the stove out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. Don't put clothing or anything flammable on or near it.
  • Don't run it with the front door open or ajar, and don't slam or strike the glass.
  • Burn only natural gas or propane, never wood, paper, cardboard or coal.
If any part has been under water, don't use the stove. Call a qualified service technician to inspect it and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that was under water.

service.title: Cleaning and yearly service
service.html:
The stove and its vent system must be inspected every year by a qualified gas technician. Always turn off the gas supply and disconnect power before any service work.

Regular care

  • Vacuum the valve compartment regularly to remove dust and debris, and more often if you have pets.
  • Keep the control compartments and the area under the stove free of dust, and the area around it clear of anything that burns.
  • Make sure nothing blocks the flow of air through the firebox, valve compartment, convection airways and optional blower.
  • Clean both sides of the safety screens now and then with a fine, soft-bristle brush or a vacuum attachment. Use only very gentle pressure.
  • Use a soft brush attachment around the logs and handle them carefully.

Every year

  • The whole vent system is inspected. If it's taken apart, it must be resealed to the vent maker's instructions, never with silicone.
  • A qualified technician inspects and cleans the pilot assembly and burner base and replaces anything corroded.
  • The glass gasket is checked for wear and a good seal.
Lint from carpeting, bedding and the like can mean you need to clean more often.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser against defects in material and workmanship, from the date of purchase.

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, ceramic burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas and electrical parts (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

Not covered

  • Normal wear parts: lamp bulbs, paint, gaskets and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress)
  • Damage from incorrect installation, or from unauthorized modification, use or repair
  • Enamel damage from misuse, such as bubbling, cracking or discoloration
  • Travel costs, and damage in transit

Making a claim

Contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer. Jøtul must hear about a possible defect within 60 days of when it was first discovered, or reasonably could have been. Keep your dated sales receipt. You arrange, at your own expense, getting the part to and from the dealer. The warranty isn't transferable. It's void if installation or service is done by someone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier, or if installation doesn't follow the manual or local and national fire and building regulations.

This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

Note: p. 4 pairs the propane minimum inlet pressure of 11.0 WC with 3.0 kPa, and the two figures don't match; the inlet pressure table on p. 19 gives 11.0 in. WC.

Manometer on test point B (inlet / supply) on the front of the valve; always test with the valve control knob set on HIGH. The suggested tools list includes an external regulator for propane only (p. 2).

Disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve from the supply piping during pressure tests above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve for tests at or below 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).

specManifold.html:
NG min / max1.6 / 3.50 WC (.40 / .87 kPa)
LP min / max6.4 / 10.0 WC (1.59 / 2.49 kPa)

Test point A (manifold) on the front of the valve, valve control knob set on HIGH.

Pilot flame: steady, not lifting or floating; blue around the pilot hood with traces of yellow toward the outer edges; engulfs the top 1/8" of the flame sensor and projects toward the burner carry-over ports. The pilot adjustment screw is left of the valve regulator; qualified technician only.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Every termination must fall in the shaded area of the vent matrix, which is a diagram (fig. 6.2, p. 10). Set the exhaust restrictor to that termination zone (A–D); see the vent install step.

Vertical termination

Max horizontal run20 ft. (152 cm)
Min vertical termination6 ft. (183 cm)
Total run incl. offsets35 ft. (10.67m) max
Cap discharge openings18 in. (457 mm) min horizontally from roof surface
Note: for vertical termination, p. 11 prints the maximum horizontal run as 20 ft. (152 cm), and the two figures don't match. The horizontal termination section on the same page gives 20 ft. (6.1 m); p. 12 gives 5 ft. (152.4 cm) as the maximum horizontal run at minimum vertical run.

Firestop at every floor, opening framed 10" X 10" inside. Wall straps every three feet on offsets. Enclose venting exposed in living space above the first floor; keep 1" from all sides; retain attic insulation with a barrier. Co-linear termination: 2 foot max horizontal run.

Horizontal termination

Min vertical rise24" (61 cm)
Max vertical run35 ft. (10.67m)
Max horizontal run20 ft. (6.1 m)
At minimum vertical run5 ft. (152.4 cm) max horizontal
Snorkel, 14" or 36"2 ft. max horizontal run
Wall cut-out, combustible wall10" X 10" min

Elbows: up to two 45° or one 90° in addition to the first elbow; cut the horizontal run 5 feet for each additional elbow. Horizontal runs level or rising 1/4 in. per foot toward the cap, never downward. A 14" snorkel needs 12" of vent off the stove to meet the minimum rise. Cap: 3" to overhead combustible projections of 2 1/2" or less, 12" to projections over 2 1/2"; not recessed into a wall or siding; vinyl siding standoff (M&G Dura-Vent #950) on vinyl siding. Exterior terminal clearances for Canada and the U.S. are in the table on p. 13.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Rear, from rear shroud2" (51 mm)
Side, from side plate7 3/8" (178 mm)
Corner, from side plate3 3/8" (86 mm)
Ceiling, from top plate33 1/2" (850 mm)
Note: p. 7 prints the side clearance as 7 3/8" with 178 mm, and the two figures don't match; the manual gives no other side clearance.

Vent pipe to combustibles

Horizontal run, top2" (51 mm)
Horizontal run, sides and bottom1" (25 mm)
Vertical run, all sides1" (25 mm)

Don't fill the clearance air space around the vent pipe with any type of insulation (p. 12).

Floor protection

Never directly on carpeting, vinyl or linoleum. On any combustible floor other than wood: metal, wood, ceramic tile, stone or a listed hearth pad, the full width and depth of the appliance (carpet, vinyl, linoleum or laminate can stay underneath). "Fire resistant" materials and "fire-rated" sheet rock count as combustible. Floor, parallel and corner clearances are drawn as diagrams (figs. 5.1–5.3).

specConv.html:
Ships for natural gas. Convert with the supplied Propane Conversion Kit 158057; revert with Natural Gas Conversion Kit 158058. An authorized service technician installs the kit (in Canada, per the provincial authorities and the CAN1-B149.1 and .2 code).

LP orifice1.45 mm

Kit contents: regulator tower labeled LP, LP orifice, pilot injector, #8 x 1/2" sheet metal screw, Label A (lower door hinge), Label B (rating plate), small valve label, instructions. Tools: 1/2" or 13 mm wrench or deep-well socket, Torx T20, 1/4" socket driver or spade screwdriver, 7/16" open-end wrench, small pliers or vice-grip.

High altitude: if the gas supplier does not derate above 2000 feet, fit kit 158059 (propane) or 158060 (NG) and apply the completed high altitude label to the rating plate.

conflicts.issue: What the Mode switch ON position does: pp. 26 and 28 say ON lights the pilot and then the burner, which stays on until manually switched OFF; the lighting instructions on p. 45 say ON is for continuous pilot operation, with the burner lit from the remote transmitter.

After the automatic 7-day pilot shut-off: p. 27 says the pilot converts to IPI and re-ignites at the next call for heat (p. 45 also says it re-ignites automatically); p. 28 says to follow the Lighting Instructions to relight the pilot.
Backup battery box location: left side of the controls compartment (p. 5) vs right side control compartment (p. 34).

Factory NG air shutter setting: specifications give NG 0" / LP 1/16" (p. 4); fuel conversion step 16 says the factory setting for NG is 1/16" open (p. 18). Adjustment start point and run time also differ: 1/16" open and at least 15 minutes (p. 18) vs mid-point of range and 20-30 minutes on HIGH (p. 24).
Log set numbering: the contents list gives #2 Left Log 226265 and #3 Right Log 226266, but the install steps say Right Log #2 and Left Log #3.

Maximum horizontal run for vertical termination is printed as 20 ft. (152 cm) (p. 11), and the two units don't match; the horizontal termination section on the same page gives 20 ft. (6.1 m), and p. 12 (fig. 6.8 text) gives 5 ft. (152.4 cm) as the maximum horizontal run at minimum vertical run. The vent matrix that would settle the vertical-termination limit (fig. 6.2, p. 10) is a diagram with garbled text. A venting limit, so shown as printed with a note rather than corrected; the vent card's 20 ft. row is labeled horizontal termination.

Side clearance (from side plate) printed as 7 3/8" (178 mm); the inch and metric figures don't match, while the other clearances' metric figures match their inch figures. No other page gives a side clearance.

Propane minimum inlet pressure printed as 11.0 WC (3.0 kPa) on p. 4; the two figures don't match, while every other p. 4 kPa figure matches its WC figure. The p. 19 inlet pressure table gives 11.0 (inches water column) with no kPa figure.

Weak flame and the air shutter: p. 24 says to increase the air shutter opening if the flame appears weak, slow or sooty; the same page says too large an air setting gives a blue and transparent, or 'anemic', flame; p. 9 says overly strong draft can cause poor combustion and a weak flame picture. The fault panel (retitled 'Blue, transparent flame') points to the step8 note.

catalog_mismatches.manual: described as the optional blower fan (p. 2) and optional blower (p. 31)

review.notes: Manual is 139894 Rev 6 dated 9/22 (file name says Rev. 7). Catalog BTU inputs, CSA P.4.1-15 efficiencies (67.91% NG / 68.53% LP), IPI/CPI ignition and mobile-home approval match the manual. Dimensions appear only in Figure 1.1 (p. 4) as a drawing; the text gives no weight, heating area or vent pipe diameters (only an Adapter Pipe, 6.625 dia, part 129322, in the p. 37 parts list), so catalog height/width/depth, weight, heating area and vent_size could not be checked. No LED/flash code table (only a red IFC LED for low backup battery and a yellow LED during remote sync), so codes is empty. No troubleshooting chart: fault panels come from the flame-appearance text (p. 24), IPI rectification and draft notes (pp. 11, 15, 27), propane sooting (p. 21) and pilot carry-over (p. 22). Diagram-only content not transcribed: vent restriction zone matrix fig. 6.2 (p. 10, garbled), mantel/ceiling clearances fig. 5.5 (p. 8, garbled callouts), floor/corner figs. 5.1-5.3 (p. 7; callouts 18" (457 mm) and 18" (475 mm) unexplained), vent figs. 6.7-6.10 (p. 12), flame pattern photos (p. 41), wiring schematic (p. 35). The terminal clearance table (p. 13) has interleaved Canada/U.S. columns and inconsistent metric (e.g. 12 in. (46 cm)), so it is referenced, not transcribed. Battery replacement step 2 on p. 34 says 'Remove the cast iron overlay', which looks carried over from another model; kept as printed. p. 5 points to fig. 16.4, p. 33 for the battery box, but the battery box is fig. 16.6, p. 34. p. 29 says setting the stove 'Pilot Mode switch' to IPI disables remote IPI/CPI switching, though the stove switch is otherwise described only as ON/OFF/REMOTE; left out of the owner text. Parts of the p. 28 remote text are font-garbled (MODE key component list, 'return to full Manual functionality' steps) and were not used. p. 24 says to open the shutter if the flame looks weak, while describing an 'anemic' flame as too much air; shown as a note in step8 and recorded in review.conflicts. Replacement safety screens are 158062 front / 158063 side (pp. 6, 39); p. 33 heads the front procedure with 225950 (front screen assembly, p. 37). The valve is called 'Sit 886' on p. 27 and SIT .885.001 in the p. 38 parts list (not used in the guide).
